2.1 For a finite separated compound $A$ with factors $(t_\ell i_\ell,x_\ell)$, define $S(A):=\sum_\ell t_\ell S_{i_\ell}(x_\ell)$. The sum is finite and invariant under reordering; concatenating compounds adds the sums, and scaling every amount by $t>0$ multiplies it by $t$. The explicit-factor convention in the Statement therefore makes $S$ well-defined, additive, and extensive. [A1, step 1.1, construct]

3.1 Fix a composition with amounts $M_i$ for finitely many labels and let $A,B$ be two states of that same composition. For a state $x$ of type $i$, put
$s_i(x):=\frac{S_i(x)-S_i(a_i)}{\mu_i}.$
The same-type entropy representation and the CH for type $i$ show
$\iota(x)\sim_s(1-s_i(x))\iota(a_i)+s_i(x)\iota(b_i).$
Indeed, the signed difference has total coefficient zero and $S_i$-value zero, so its positive and negative parts have equal mass and entropy and therefore compare both ways by [F2]. The calibrator relation gives
$(\iota(b_i)-\iota(a_i))\sim_s(\iota(d_i)-\iota(c_i))$
by taking the signed difference of $(a_i,d_i)\sim(b_i,c_i)$ and canceling common terms with [F3]. Add and scale these identities over the finitely many factors of $A$. With
$q_i(A):=\sum_{\ell:\,i_\ell=i}t_\ell s_i(x_\ell),$
the resulting signed map is
$A\sim_s \sum_i M_i \iota(a_i)+\sum_i q_i(A)(\iota(d_i)-\iota(c_i)),$
where the sums range over the finite support of the composition. The same holds for $B$. Since they have the same composition, the reference base cancels, and $B-A$ is signed-equivalent to the finite meter map
$D:=\sum_i\bigl(q_i(B)-q_i(A)\bigr)(\iota(d_i)-\iota(c_i)).$
Extend the meter entropy linearly to raw finite signed coefficient maps using density $S_m(z)/w_{\Gamma_m}$ at a meter raw tag $(\Gamma_m,z)$; in particular its value on $\iota(z)$ is $S_m(z)$. Then
$S_m(D)=\sum_i\bigl(q_i(B)-q_i(A)\bigr)\mu_i=S(B)-S(A).$
The positive and negative parts of $D$ have equal mass. If $S(A)\le S(B)$, the same-type entropy representation [F2] for finite meter products gives $D^-\prec D^+$, hence $D$ compares in the forward signed direction. Translation, addition, and ordinary-order compatibility [F3] transfer this to $A\prec B$. Conversely, if $A\prec B$, the same signed equivalences and translation in [F3] give $D^-\prec D^+$. The meter representation in [F2] then forces $S_m(D)=S(B)-S(A)\ge0$. Reversing the entropy inequality gives the reverse comparison. Thus $S$ characterizes every same-composition comparison. Each particular comparison uses only finitely many labels; no infinite sum or uncountable product occurs. [A1, F1, F2, F3, step 1.1, step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 The meter normalization fixes the multiplicative unit. Changing the chosen reference state for type $i$ changes only its additive constant; on a finite compound these constants contribute amount-weighted conserved-type offsets. This proves the stated freedom and completes the construction. [A1, step 1.1, step 2.1, algebra] ∎

## Definition

Let $\mathcal G$ be a set of tagged system types closed under finite composition $T\times T'$ and positive scaling $tT$. Scaling is associative and acts componentwise on products: $s(tT)=(st)T$ and $t(T\times T')=(tT)\times(tT')$. Each type $T$ has a nonempty state set $X_T$ of finite tagged compounds, every state in $X_T$ is represented by the coefficient-map interpretation of [[def-tdmath-forward-sector-hypotheses]] and has total coefficient mass $m(T)=w_T\ge0$, and $m(T\times T')=m(T)+m(T')$, $m(tT)=t\,m(T)$. The entropy $\sigma_T:X_T\to\mathbb R$ is the finite additive extensive entropy from [[thm-tdmath-arbitrary-family-calibration]]; in particular $\sigma_{tT}(ta)=t\sigma_T(a)$.

Include the formal empty unit type $1$, with $X_1=\{*\}$, $m(1)=0$, $\sigma_1(*)=0$, $T\times1=T$, and $t1=1$. A transition edge from type $T$ to type $T'$ is a pair $a\in X_T$, $b\in X_{T'}$ such that the underlying equal-mass compounds satisfy $a\prec b$ under [[def-tdmath-forward-sector-hypotheses]]. Thus an edge can exist only when $m(T)=m(T')$. Its cost is the finite real number $\sigma_{T'}(b)-\sigma_T(a)$.

A decorated finite chain from $\Gamma$ to $\Gamma'$ consists of a catalyst type $C\in\mathcal G$, an integer $N\ge1$, types $T_0=\Gamma\times C,T_1,\ldots,T_N=\Gamma'\times C$, and states $a_k\in X_{T_k}$, $b_{k+1}\in X_{T_{k+1}}$ with an edge $a_k\prec b_{k+1}$ for every $0\le k<N$. Its cost is the finite real sum

$$c=\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}\bigl(\sigma_{T_{k+1}}(b_{k+1})-\sigma_{T_k}(a_k)\bigr).$$

Define $F(\Gamma,\Gamma')$ as the infimum of all such witness costs. Set $F=+\infty$ if there is no witness and $F=-\infty$ if the witness costs are unbounded below. The infimum is over real witness costs, so no subtraction of extended-real infima is used. Type permutations, reassociation, reversible identifications, and the identity $T\times1=T$ are part of the declared type structure. The cost identities and inequalities require a separate proof.

A cross-type mixing and reaction network consists of a declared set $\mathcal G$ of tagged composition types, a state set $X_\Gamma$ for each $\Gamma\in\mathcal G$, and a set of channel-labelled process records. A record $P$ for a channel $\alpha$ has an equilibrium initial state $x^-_P\in X_\Gamma$, an equilibrium final state $x^+_P\in X_{\Gamma'}$, and the full protocol, outer-boundary, energy and auxiliary data needed for that channel. Define $(\Gamma,x)\mathcal R(\Gamma',y)$ exactly when at least one admitted channel record has those endpoint states. No channel is inferred from separated composition.

For any permitted equal-formal-mass compound states $A,B$ of the network, define $A\prec B$ exactly when at least one admitted channel record has initial state $A$ and final state $B$; for named single types this is the relation $\mathcal R$ above. This is the exact relation supplied to [[def-tdmath-forward-sector-hypotheses]], not a separate abstract order that enlarges or restricts the channel edges. Its extension to finite tagged products and common spectators is governed by the adopted A1–A6 conditions below. Thus every edge in a decorated chain is precisely an admitted channel transition. This identification is a declared model condition.

The network is **finite-factor closed** when its types admit the declared finite composition and positive scaling operations and each allowed channel respects the model’s stated conservation constraints. In addition, each channel must preserve the dimensionless formal mass $m$ of [[def-td-scaled-products-and-comparison]]; this is the equal-coefficient-mass convention required by the mathematical chain-cost supplier, not a statement that formal mass is kilograms or moles. $$F(\Gamma,\Gamma')<+\infty\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad F(\Gamma',\Gamma)<+\infty.$$

No-sinks is an explicit property required of a network used in the global-offset theorem; it is not proved by this definition, and it is not asserted for every physical mixing or reaction. The definition permits the channel set to be empty; then the condition must still be checked rather than inferred.

## Definition

A finite rate model consists of a finite nonempty state set $S$ and rates $q_{ij}\ge0$ in seconds$^{-1}$ for $i\ne j$. Set $q_{ii}=-\sum_{j\ne i}q_{ij}$. A row probability vector is $p=(p_i)_{i\in S}$ with $p_i\ge0$ and $\sum_i p_i=1$. Its time-dependent law $p(t)$ follows the continuous-time master equation $\dot p_i=\sum_{j\ne i}[p_jq_{ji}-p_iq_{ij}]$. A strictly positive normalized vector $\pi$ is a detailed-balance law when $\pi_iq_{ij}=\pi_jq_{ji}$ for every distinct pair. Its undirected rate graph has an edge $\{i,j\}$ exactly when $\pi_iq_{ij}>0$; detailed balance makes this equivalent to $\pi_jq_{ji}>0$.

For a discrete transition kernel $K$ on a finite state set, $\pi$-detailed balance means $\pi_iK(i,j)=\pi_jK(j,i)$ for every pair. If $\pi$ is strictly positive, this identity pairs the supports of forward and reversed transitions. A rate model or a reversible kernel is a mathematical/physical model class; no observed trajectory is asserted by the definition.

## Definition

A finite statistical microstate model is a pair $(\Omega,\epsilon)$ where $\Omega$ is a finite nonempty set and $\epsilon:\Omega\to\mathbb R$ assigns a finite numerical energy to each microstate. ## Definition

Take $\Omega$ to be a finite nonempty microstate set as in [[def-td-finite-microstate-model]]: distinct elements count as distinct microstates, and the physical energy values are finite and measured in joules in the declared rest frame. The finite partition sum and canonical probability vector at stage $k$ are $Z_k=\sum_{i\in\Omega}e^{-\beta E_k(i)}$ and $\pi_k(i)=e^{-\beta E_k(i)}/Z_k$. Since $\Omega$ is nonempty and finite and each energy is finite, $0<Z_k<\infty$ and $\pi_k$ is a strictly positive probability vector.

A transition kernel at stage $k$ is a matrix $K_k(i,j)\ge0$ with $\sum_{j\in\Omega}K_k(i,j)=1$. In the forward stage order, the energy changes instantaneously from $E_{k-1}$ to $E_k$ while the state is still $i_{k-1}$; the subsequent bath transition samples $i_k$ using $K_k(i_{k-1},i_k)$ at fixed energy $E_k$. A path is $\omega=(i_0,\ldots,i_m)\in\Omega^{m+1}$. For an initial law $\mu_0$, its path probability is $P_F(\omega)=\mu_0(i_0)\prod_{k=1}^mK_k(i_{k-1},i_k)$.

Work on the system is positive when energy is supplied to it, and heat into the system is positive when a bath transition raises its energy. Define $W(\omega)=\sum_{k=1}^m[E_k(i_{k-1})-E_{k-1}(i_{k-1})]$ and $Q_{\mathrm{in}}(\omega)=\sum_{k=1}^m[E_k(i_k)-E_k(i_{k-1})]$, both in joules. Define $F_k=-\beta^{-1}\log Z_k$ and $\Delta F=F_m-F_0=-\beta^{-1}\log(Z_m/Z_0)$. These are finite-model quantities; their physical interpretation is conditional on the adopted preparation and transition assumptions.

## Statement

Let $M$ and $R$ take values in finite sets under a joint probability law $p(m,r)\ge0$ with $\sum_{m,r}p(m,r)=1$. For any finite random variable $Y$ with law $p_Y$, define its Shannon entropy by $H(Y):=-\sum_{y:p_Y(y)>0}p_Y(y)\log p_Y(y)$; for a pair, $H(M,R)$ means this definition applied to its joint law. Put $a_r:=\sum_m p(m,r)$ and, when $a_r>0$, $q(m|r):=p(m,r)/a_r$. Thus $H(R)=-\sum_{r:a_r>0}a_r\log a_r$. Define $H(M|R):=\sum_{r:a_r>0}a_r[-\sum_{m:q(m|r)>0}q(m|r)\log q(m|r)]$. Then $H(M,R)=H(R)+H(M|R)$ and $H(M|R)\ge0$.

This is a specified regular field class on a fixed rigid body. It does not assert that every physical medium has local-equilibrium fields, nor does it adopt a heat equation, a boundary condition, Fourier's law, or an entropy-production law.

## Definition

Fix $d\ge2$. The **elastic collision set** is
$$Q_{\rm el}:=\{(v,w,v',w')\in\mathbb R^{4d}:v+w=v'+w',\ |v|^2+|w|^2=|v'|^2+|w'|^2\},$$
with its relative Borel sigma-algebra. A collision measure is a nonnegative countably additive measure $\nu$ on this measurable space. It is symmetric if it is invariant under the exchanges $(v,w)\leftrightarrow(w,v)$, $(v',w')\leftrightarrow(w',v')$, and $(v,w)\leftrightarrow(v',w')$. These invariances are hypotheses on $\nu$, not consequences of energy and momentum conservation.

For a positive function $f:\mathbb R^d\to(0,\infty)$, write $Q(f)$ for a collision operator when the following **weak collision identity** holds for each test function $\varphi$ used:
$$\int_{\mathbb R^d}\varphi(v)Q(f)(v)\,dv=\frac14\int_{Q_{\rm el}}(f(v')f(w')-f(v)f(w))(\varphi(v)+\varphi(w)-\varphi(v')-\varphi(w'))\,d\nu,$$
with absolute convergence. This identity is the adopted mathematical collision model. Molecular chaos or a microscopic derivation of it is not part of the definition.

## Scope

The measure's normalization is chosen so $Q(f)$ has units of $f$ per unit time in an application. No specific cross-section or measured collision rate is asserted.

## Definition

Fix a particle mass $m_p>0$ in kilograms and velocity space $V=\mathbb R^3$ with components in $\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$. The elastic collision set is
$$Q_{\rm el}=\{(v,w,v',w')\in V^4:v+w=v'+w',\ |v|^2+|w|^2=|v'|^2+|w'|^2\}.$$
Thus each allowed event conserves momentum $m_p(v+w)$ and kinetic energy $m_p(|v|^2+|w|^2)/2$. Equip $Q_{\rm el}$ with the Borel sets generated by its relative topology.

Collision-rate data consist of a nonnegative, countably additive, $\sigma$-finite Borel measure $\nu$ on these Borel sets. It is invariant under exchanging $v$ with $w$, exchanging $v'$ with $w'$, and exchanging the incoming pair $(v,w)$ with the outgoing pair $(v',w')$: for each of these maps $S$ and Borel set $E$, $\nu(S^{-1}E)=\nu(E)$. This is the three-dimensional physical restriction of the collision set and exchange conventions in [[def-tdmath-elastic-collision-kernel]], with $\sigma$-finiteness stated explicitly for the product integrals used by the entropy theorem. Its physical units and rate normalization are chosen so the associated weak collision operator has units of density per second. The measure is a declared model input; no differential cross section or microscopic limit is inferred from this Definition.

## Definition

Let $O\subset\mathbb R^m$, $m\ge2$, be open, let $H\in C^2(O,\mathbb R)$, and let $J\subset\mathbb R$ be open. An energy $E\in J$ is **regular** if $\nabla H(x)\ne0$ for every $x\in\Sigma_E:=H^{-1}(\{E\})$. By the implicit-function theorem, a neighborhood of each point of a nonempty regular level is a graph $x_i=h(z)$.

In a graph chart, use the local area density $\sqrt{1+|\nabla h(z)|^2}\,dz$, where $dz$ is $(m-1)$-dimensional Lebesgue measure. A **graph partition** on $\Sigma_E$ is a locally finite graph-chart cover with nonnegative smooth functions $\chi_a$ supported in their respective charts and summing to one on the level. Whenever such a partition is supplied, define the candidate weighted shell integral by
$$\mu_E(g):=\sum_a\int g(z,h_a(z))\chi_a(z,h_a(z))|\partial_iH(z,h_a(z))|^{-1}\,dz$$
for nonnegative Borel $g$. Its independence from the chosen chart partition, and its equality with $\int_{\Sigma_E}g|\nabla H|^{-1}dA_E$, are proved in the theorem on this page. If $0<\mu_E(1)<\infty$, the **microcanonical shell probability** is $\widehat\mu_E:=\mu_E/\mu_E(1)$.

This is an explicit chart-based definition, not a formal delta distribution $\delta(H-E)$. Critical levels are excluded.

## Statement

Assume AC. Let $O\subset\mathbb R^{2n}$ be open with its canonical symplectic form, let $H\in C^2(O,\mathbb R)$, and let $J\subset\mathbb R$ be open. Suppose $\nabla H\ne0$ on $H^{-1}(J)$ and $H^{-1}(K)$ is compact in $O$ for every compact $K\subset J$. Define $\mu_E$ by [[def-tdmath-regular-energy-shell]]. Then for every nonnegative Borel $f$ compactly supported in $H^{-1}(J)$,
$$\int_Of(x)\,dx=\int_J\mu_E(f)\,dE.$$
For every $E\in J$ with nonempty shell $\Sigma_E=H^{-1}(\{E\})$, $0<\mu_E(1)<\infty$, and $\widehat\mu_E=\mu_E/\mu_E(1)$ is a probability measure. Let $\phi_t$ be a Hamiltonian flow map defined as a diffeomorphism on a full compact energy band containing $\Sigma_E$ and preserving that band. Then $\widehat\mu_E$ is invariant under $\phi_t$ for every such regular $E$. Critical levels and noncompact bands are outside this statement.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The regular-band data, the weighted-area definition, and the complete Hamiltonian flow on the particular band.

[A1] AC is adopted; $O\subset\mathbb R^{2n}$ is open, $H\in C^2$, $\nabla H\ne0$ on $H^{-1}(J)$, and compact energy intervals have compact inverse images in $O$.

[A2] The nonnegative Borel function is compactly supported in $H^{-1}(J)$. For invariance, $\phi_t$ is a diffeomorphism on a compact band, maps it onto itself, and is the Hamiltonian flow of $H$.

[F1] [[def-axiom-of-choice]] and [[def-tdmath-regular-energy-shell]]: AC is the standing hypothesis of the change-of-variables supplier; the candidate shell integral is the sum over a supplied graph partition, and graph area in a chart has density $\sqrt{1+|\nabla h|^2}\,dz$.

[F2] [[thm-euclidean-implicit-function-theorem]]: if one partial derivative of $H$ is nonzero, a neighborhood of that level is a $C^1$ graph $x_i=h(z,E)$ with $\partial_Eh=1/\partial_iH$.

[F3] [[thm-c-one-change-of-variables-for-nonnegative-lebesgue-measurable-functions]]: a $C^1$ injective change of variables with nonzero Jacobian transforms a nonnegative Lebesgue integral by the absolute Jacobian.

[F4] [[thm-tonelli-theorem-for-sigma-finite-product-spaces]] and [[def-lebesgue-measure-and-the-lebesgue-sigma-algebra]]: nonnegative chart integrals may be interchanged and decomposed over Euclidean Lebesgue factors.

[F5] [[thm-tdmath-hamiltonian-measure-and-recurrence]]: on the domain of a Hamiltonian flow, the canonical symplectic volume is preserved and $H$ is constant along each orbit.

[F6] [[thm-dominated-convergence]]: a common integrable chart bound justifies continuity in $E$ of compactly supported shell integrals.

[F7] [[lem-distance-to-set-is-lipschitz]] and [[thm-metric-closure-characterisation]]: distance to a nonempty closed set is continuous and vanishes exactly on that set.

[F8] [[lem-finite-measure-uniqueness-on-a-pi-system]]: two finite measures that agree on a generating pi-system and have equal total mass agree on the generated sigma-algebra.

## Proof



**Given:** [A1]–[A2] and the geometric and measure interfaces [F1]–[F7].

1.1 Let $C$ be a compact energy band containing the support of $f$. At each $x\in H^{-1}(C)$, some coordinate derivative $\partial_iH(x)$ is nonzero. By [F2] a neighborhood is parameterized by the remaining coordinates $z$ and energy $E$, with $x_i=h(z,E)$. Compactness gives a finite cover by such charts. Refine the cover by finitely many balls whose closures lie in chart domains and whose smaller concentric balls cover $H^{-1}(C)$. Choose standard smooth bump functions $\psi_a$ supported in the larger balls and positive on the smaller balls, and let $\Psi=\sum_a\psi_a$. Its minimum on $H^{-1}(C)$ is positive. Choose a smooth scalar cutoff $\eta$ that is zero below one quarter of this minimum and one above one half of it. Then $\chi_a=\eta(\Psi)\psi_a/\Psi$, extended by zero where $\Psi=0$, is smooth, supported in its chart, and the sum is one near $H^{-1}(C)$. [A1, A2, F2, F4, construct]

2.1 In each chart, the map $(z,E)\mapsto(z,h_a(z,E))$ is injective after shrinking the chart, and its absolute Jacobian is $|\partial_Eh_a|=|\partial_iH|^{-1}$. By [F3] and Tonelli [F4], $$\int_O f(x)\chi_a(x)\,dx =\int_J\int f(z,h_a(z,E))\chi_a(z,h_a(z,E))|\partial_iH|^{-1}\,dz\,dE.$$ Implicit differentiation gives $\partial_{z_j}h_a=-\partial_jH/\partial_iH$, so the graph area density is $$\sqrt{1+|\nabla_zh_a|^2}\,dz=\frac{|\nabla H|}{|\partial_iH|}\,dz.$$ The inner integral is therefore the corresponding chart contribution to the candidate $\mu_E(f)$ in [F1]. Sum the finitely many charts and use $\sum_a\chi_a=1$ on the support to obtain the asserted coarea identity. [A1, A2, F1, F2, F3, F4, step 1.1, algebra]

2.2 On overlaps, if one graph parameterization is obtained from another by a $C^1$ coordinate change $\psi$, its Gram matrix is transformed by $G\mapsto(D\psi)^\top G(D\psi)$. Taking determinants shows the area density changes by $|\det D\psi|$, exactly the ordinary chart Jacobian. Implicit differentiation gives $\sqrt{1+|\nabla h|^2}/|\nabla H|=|\partial_iH|^{-1}$, so the chart contributions define the same measure independent of the partition and equal $\int_{\Sigma_E}g|\nabla H|^{-1}dA_E$. Each shell is a closed subset of compact $H^{-1}(\{E\})$, hence compact. A finite collection of graph charts with $\nabla H$ bounded away from zero on that compact level gives finite area and hence $\mu_E(1)<\infty$. If the shell is nonempty, one graph chart contains an open patch; its coordinate domain has positive $(2n-1)$-dimensional measure and the continuous density $|\nabla H|^{-1}dA_E/dz$ is positive there, so $\mu_E(1)>0$. [A1, F1, F2, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 Fix a compact band and a compactly supported continuous test $g$ on it. For a continuous compactly supported scalar function $q$ on $J$, the coarea identity from 1.2 and the Hamiltonian volume/energy invariance [F5] give $$\int_Jq(E)\mu_E(g\circ\phi_t)\,dE =\int_Oq(H(x))g(\phi_tx)\,dx =\int_Oq(H(x))g(x)\,dx =\int_Jq(E)\mu_E(g)\,dE.$$ The second equality is the change of variables by the volume-preserving diffeomorphism $\phi_t$; $H\circ\phi_t=H$ keeps the energy weight fixed. For each test $g$, both functions of $E$ in the outer integrals are continuous locally: use the finite chart representation in 1.2, compact chart support, the positive lower bound for $|\nabla H|$, and dominated convergence [F6]. Their difference integrates to zero against every compactly supported continuous $q$. If the continuous difference were nonzero at one energy, it would keep one strict sign on a neighborhood; a nonnegative continuous bump $q$ supported there would make the integral nonzero. Thus $\mu_E(g\circ\phi_t)=\mu_E(g)$ for every $E$ in the band. [A1, A2, F1, F5, F6, step 2.1]

4.1 Fix a closed subset $F$ of a nonempty shell. If $F=\varnothing$, both measures assign it zero. Otherwise let $\chi$ be a continuous compactly supported cutoff equal to one on the compact shell; the same finite-ball bump construction used in 1.1 supplies it. In the ambient band set $g_n(x)=\chi(x)\max\{0,1-n\,\operatorname{dist}(x,F)\}$. By [F7], $g_n$ is continuous, $0\le g_n\le1$, and its restriction to $\Sigma_E$ converges pointwise to $\mathbf1_F$. Because $\phi_t$ maps the shell onto itself, $g_n\circ\phi_t$ converges there to $\mathbf1_{\phi_t^{-1}F}$. Apply 2.1 to each $g_n$ and use dominated convergence [F6] for the finite shell measure from 1.3; this gives $\mu_E(\phi_t^{-1}F)=\mu_E(F)$ for every closed $F\subseteq\Sigma_E$. Closed sets form a pi-system generating the shell Borel sigma-algebra, and both $\mu_E$ and its pushforward have the same finite total mass because $\phi_t$ maps the shell onto itself. [F5, F6, F7, step 2.2, step 3.1]

5.1 By [F8], agreement on closed sets and equality of total masses imply that $\mu_E$ equals its pushforward on every Borel subset of $\Sigma_E$. Divide by $0<\mu_E(1)<\infty$ from 1.3. Hence the normalized regular-shell probability is invariant for each such $E$, not merely almost every energy. [F8, step 2.2, step 4.1] ∎

## Definition

Fix an integer $n\ge1$, a canonical chart with physical coordinates $q_i$ in metres and $p_i$ in $\mathrm{kg\,m\,s^{-1}}$, and the corresponding dimensionless coordinates $\hat q_i=q_i/(1\,\mathrm m)$ and $\hat p_i=p_i/(1\,\mathrm{kg\,m\,s^{-1}})$. Let $O\subseteq\mathbb R^{2n}$ be the open domain of the numerical vector $\hat x=(\hat q,\hat p)$, let $\hat H:O\to\mathbb R$ be the numerical energy map with physical energy $H=(1\,\mathrm J)\hat H$, and require $\hat H$ to have continuous partial derivatives through order two. A specified open interval $J_E\subseteq\mathbb R$ is a regular compact-shell band when $\hat H^{-1}(K)$ is compact in $O$ for every compact $K\subset J_E$ and $\nabla\hat H$ is nonzero at every point of $\hat H^{-1}(J_E)$.

For $\hat E\in J_E$, the energy shell is $\Sigma_{\hat E}:=\{x\in O:\hat H(x)=\hat E\}$. The graph-chart definition of the weighted shell integral is [[def-tdmath-regular-energy-shell]]: in a local graph chart $x_i=h(z,\hat E)$, its coarea measure is $d\mu_{\hat E}=dA_{\hat E}/|\nabla\hat H|$, with graph-area factor and gradient in the dimensionless Euclidean coordinates. Set $D(\hat E):=\int_{\Sigma_{\hat E}}d\mu_{\hat E}$ and admit the preparation only when $\Sigma_{\hat E}\ne\varnothing$ and $0<D(\hat E)<\infty$. Its normalized shell law is $\nu_{\hat E}(A):=D(\hat E)^{-1}\mu_{\hat E}(A\cap\Sigma_{\hat E})$. The current draft theorem [[thm-tdmath-regular-energy-shell-measure]] proves the coarea identity, chart independence and positive finite shell mass under its stated $C^2$, compact-regular-band hypotheses; its statement and proof are present, while its acceptance remains unresolved. Multiplying the unnormalized shell measure by a fixed positive phase-volume normalization does not change $\nu_{\hat E}$.

## Definition

Fix a working system of constitution $c$ and a closed process record $P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{cl}}(c)$ with equilibrium endpoints as in [[def-td-process-and-protocol]]. A cycle of the working system is such a record with $x_P^-=x_P^+$; the reservoirs and work store need not return to their initial energy states.

An ideal thermal reservoir $b$ has an energy interval $J_b\subseteq\mathbb R$ measured in joules and a finite entropy function $S_b:J_b\to\mathbb R$ measured in $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$. On the energy interval admitted for a cycle, assume the exact affine law
$
S_b(E_b)=s_{b,0}+\frac{E_b}{T_b}
$
for a constant $s_{b,0}$ and fixed $T_b>0$ kelvins. Thus $S_b'(E_b)=1/T_b$ in the interior and every admitted endpoint change is exactly $\Delta S_b=\Delta E_b/T_b$. This constant is the absolute thermodynamic temperature under [[def-td-temperature-pressure-chemical-potential]]. The affine entropy law on the admitted interval is the ideal-bath model; a finite reservoir whose temperature changes is outside this definition.

An ideal work store is a named auxiliary with an energy coordinate $E_w$ measured in joules and an assigned entropy $S_w(E_w)=s_w$ constant on the energy interval used by the cycle. It exchanges only mechanical work and no matter or heat. Its energy may change, while its entropy change is zero by this model definition.

A two-reservoir cycle contains one working-system cycle, one hot bath at $T_h$, one cold bath at $T_c$, and the ideal work store. They lie inside one isolated outer boundary in the sense of [[def-td-system-and-permitted-exchanges]], so the full compound has no external matter or energy transfer. There are no unlisted heat, work, matter, kinetic-energy, or external-potential-energy changes. The admitted process and transfer signs are those of [[def-td-process-and-protocol]]. The model declares the endpoint entropy split
$
S_{\mathrm{tot}}=S_{\mathrm{ws}}(x_{\mathrm{ws}})+S_h(E_h)+S_{\mathrm{cold}}(E_c)+S_w(E_w),
$
where $S_{\mathrm{ws}}$ is the working-system entropy and the bath and work-store functions are those defined here. This additive constituent split is assumed to be one admitted by [[post-td-concave-fundamental-entropy]] and is the entropy supplied to [[post-td-macroscopic-second-law]]; $S_w$ contributes zero change. Reversibility of the full record is as in [[def-td-reversible-process]].

When the second law is applied to the cycle, the model also supplies an admitted closed process record for the full compound. At both endpoints its constituent preparations, with the declared contact controls locked or insulated, are an equilibrium macrostate for that record; its separately tracked center-of-mass kinetic and external-field potential energies have zero endpoint change. This total-compound record is the input to the second law; the working-system record $P$ is the input to its first-law balance.

In the heat-engine mode, the positive magnitudes $Q_h,Q_c$ in joules mean respectively heat taken from the hot bath into the working system and heat rejected by the working system to the cold bath; accordingly $\Delta E_h=-Q_h$, $\Delta E_c=Q_c$, $Q[P]=Q_h-Q_c$, and work output is $W_{\mathrm{out}}=-W_{\mathrm{on}}[P]$. In the refrigerator mode, $Q_c>0$ is heat taken from the cold bath into the working system, $Q_h>0$ is heat rejected to the hot bath, so $\Delta E_c=-Q_c$, $\Delta E_h=Q_h$, $Q[P]=Q_c-Q_h$, and work input is $W_{\mathrm{in}}=W_{\mathrm{on}}[P]$. These are idealized model conventions, not claims that a particular apparatus realizes the cycle.

## Definition

For the pair potential $\varphi$ of [[def-td-stable-tempered-continuum-preparation]], let $B=\{x\in\mathbb R^d:\varphi(x)=+\infty\}$. A finite configuration is hard-admissible if every pair displacement avoids $B$. For $z>0$, define the retained-admissibility zero-inverse-temperature weight of $\omega$ to be
$$w_0(\omega)=z^{N(\omega)}\mathbf 1_{\{H_{N(\omega)}(\omega)<\infty\}}.$$
Its finite-volume partition sum, when finite, is $\Xi_{\Lambda}^{\mathrm{ret},0}(z)=\sum_{N\geq0}\int w_0(\omega)\,\mu_{\Lambda,N}(d\omega)$, using [[post-td-classical-indistinguishable-particle-measure]]. This definition sets the weight of a forbidden configuration to zero; it does not assign a value to the undefined product $0\cdot(+\infty)$. When $B=\varnothing$ the measure is the unrestricted Poisson activity model; for a nonempty hard core it is generally not Poisson. The convention is explicit model data and carries no statement about an arbitrary zero-width energy shell.

## Definition

Let $I$ be a nonempty finite or countably infinite set equipped with a specified enumeration, let $E_i\in\mathbb R$ be finite energies, let $g_i>0$ be weights, and let $J\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an open parameter interval. For a nonnegative family $(a_i)_{i\in I}$ define $\sum_{i\in I}a_i:=\sup_{F\subset I,\,F\text{ finite}}\sum_{i\in F}a_i$, with finite sums as in [[def-finite-sum]] and the supremum as in [[def-complete-ordered-field]] when the finite subsums are bounded; set the value to $+\infty$ when they are unbounded. This definition is independent of the specified enumeration. For $\beta\in J$, define the nonnegative partition sum $Z(\beta):=\sum_{i\in I}g_i\exp(-\beta E_i)$ by this rule. The admissible parameter set is $J_Z:=\{\beta\in J:0<Z(\beta)<\infty\}$. For $\beta\in J_Z$, define $p_i(\beta):=g_i\exp(-\beta E_i)/Z(\beta)$; then $(p_i)$ is a countable probability law. For any real observable $X_i$ with $\sum_i p_i|X_i|<\infty$, define $\langle X\rangle_\beta:=\sum_i p_iX_i$. If $\sum_i|p_i\log(p_i/g_i)|<\infty$, define the reference-relative entropy $H_g(p):=-\sum_i p_i\log(p_i/g_i)$. When $g_i=1$, this is the Shannon entropy with natural logarithms. A lower bound on the energies alone is not part of this definition and does not imply $Z(\beta)<\infty$. For countably infinite $I$, any specified enumeration is used only to write a list; the nonnegative sum itself is the supremum over finite subsums above.

## Scope

The sum is interpreted using the series convention of [[def-series]]. The model is purely mathematical; any physical interpretation of $E_i$, $g_i$, or $\beta$ requires separate premises.

## Definition

A **finite-state thermodynamic-limit contract** specifies a sequence $(X_k,E_k,g_k,V_k,n_k)_{k\in\mathbb N}$, where $\mathbb N$ is the positive-integer index set of [[def-natural-numbers]], each $X_k$ is a finite nonempty state set, $E_k:X_k\to\mathbb R$ assigns finite energies in joules, $g_k:X_k\to(0,\infty)$ assigns positive dimensionless weights, $V_k>0$ is physical volume in $\mathrm{m^3}$, and, for one declared species, $n_k>0$ is its amount in moles. A fixed-density sequence has $V_k\to\infty$ and $n_k/V_k\to\rho\in(0,\infty)$ in $\mathrm{mol\,m^{-3}}$. Boundary conditions, interaction rules, and the choice of a volume or amount normalization are part of the contract and must be held fixed or explicitly tracked as $k$ varies.

For $T>0$, set $\beta:=(k_BT)^{-1}$ in $\mathrm{J^{-1}}$, with $k_B$ and units from [[def-td-si-quantities]]. The finite-state canonical partition sum is

$$
Z_k(\beta):=\sum_{x\in X_k}g_k(x)e^{-\beta E_k(x)},
$$

as the finite case of [[def-tdmath-countable-canonical-model]]. It is a positive finite real number. Define $F_k(\beta):=-\beta^{-1}\log Z_k(\beta)$ in joules and $f_k(\beta):=F_k(\beta)/V_k$ in $\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}}$. The specified thermodynamic-limit value is $f(\beta,\rho):=\lim_{k\to\infty} f_k(\beta)$ **if this limit exists**. A limit per mole or per lattice site is a different normalization and must be stated separately.

This is a contract for what a limit claim must specify, not a theorem that the limit exists. It asserts no uniformity in $\beta$, derivative interchange, ensemble equivalence, convergence rate, or nonanalyticity. A finite model's regularity and any limiting singularity require their own arguments; neither is inferred from the word “thermodynamic limit.”

## Definition

Fix integers $d\ge1$, $L\ge1$, a finite alphabet $\mathcal A$ of cardinality $q\ge1$, and a finite, possibly empty, list of interaction shapes $S_a\subset\mathbb Z^d$, each nonempty and contained in $[-R,R]^d$ for some integer $R\ge0$. $\|\Phi_a\|_\infty$ is finite because its domain is finite. For each shape let $\Phi_a:\mathcal A^{S_a}\to\mathbb R$ be a bounded interaction function. Set $J_0:=\sum_a\|\Phi_a\|_\infty$. On $\Lambda_L:=\{1,\ldots,L\}^d$, define the free-boundary energy $H_L(s):=\sum_a\sum_{x:x+S_a\subseteq\Lambda_L}\Phi_a((s_{x+u})_{u\in S_a})$, for configurations $s\in\mathcal A^{\Lambda_L}$. For $\beta>0$, define the finite partition sum $Z_L(\beta):=\sum_{s\in\mathcal A^{\Lambda_L}}e^{-\beta H_L(s)}$ and normalized log-partition density $p_L(\beta):=L^{-d}\log Z_L(\beta)$.

## Scope

The alphabet, interaction list, shapes and functions are mathematical data. The formula uses the same interaction function at every translated anchor. This definition includes free boundary conditions only; other boundary energies are introduced by an explicit bound in [[thm-tdmath-finite-range-lattice-pressure-limit]].

## Statement

For the cost $F$ of [[def-tdmath-decorated-chain-costs]], $F(\Gamma,\Gamma)=0$, $F$ is positively homogeneous, invariant under adding the same catalyst to both endpoints, and satisfies the triangle inequality whenever the extended-real sum on its right is defined. It is subadditive under composition whenever $F(\Gamma_1,\Gamma'_1)+F(\Gamma_2,\Gamma'_2)$ is defined. Every pair of actual forward and reverse decorated-chain witnesses has nonnegative total cost. A finite reverse witness therefore bounds all forward costs below; $F=-\infty$ can occur only when the reverse direction has no witness.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** A1–A6 on accessible finite compounds, the additive extensive entropy $\sigma$, and the decorated-chain definition.

[A1] [[def-tdmath-forward-sector-hypotheses]]: accessibility is reflexive, transitive, consistent under common spectators, and positively scalable; stability is available.

[F1] [[def-tdmath-decorated-chain-costs]]: each chain has a finite real cost, and $F$ is its infimum, with empty infimum $+\infty$.

[F2] [[thm-tdmath-arbitrary-family-calibration]]: $\sigma$ is additive and extensive on every separated finite compound and represents same-type comparisons.

## Proof

1.1 A reflexive identity edge from any nonempty state of $\Gamma$ to itself has cost zero, so $F(\Gamma,\Gamma)\le0$. For a decorated closed chain, start with the compound containing every edge input $a_0,\ldots,a_{N-1}$. Apply the edge $a_0\prec b_1$ with all other edge inputs as spectators, then apply $a_1\prec b_2$ with the already produced $b_1$ and all still-unused inputs as spectators, and continue through $a_{N-1}\prec b_N$. Consistency and transitivity give $\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}a_k\prec\sum_{k=1}^{N}b_k$. Since $T_N=T_0$ and the intermediate types occur once on each side, these two compounds have the same total type up to the declared reassociation and permutation. Their entropy difference is exactly the chain cost. The same-type entropy representation [F2] makes this difference nonnegative. Hence every closed-chain witness costs at least zero and $F(\Gamma,\Gamma)=0$. [A1, F1, F2, construct]

1.2 Take finite witnesses for $(\Gamma_1,\Gamma'_1)$ and $(\Gamma_2,\Gamma'_2)$. Run the first chain with a fixed state of $\Gamma_2$ and its second catalyst as spectators; then run the second chain with the first chain's output state and first catalyst as spectators. Consistency allows both sequences, and each fixed spectator contributes zero entropy difference. The resulting witness from $\Gamma_1\times\Gamma_2$ to $\Gamma'_1\times\Gamma'_2$ has the sum of the two costs. If both infima are finite real numbers, choose witnesses within $\epsilon/2$ of each infimum and let $\epsilon\downarrow0$. If one infimum is $-\infty$ and the other is finite, use a fixed finite witness for the latter and arbitrarily negative witnesses for the former; the product costs are unbounded below. If both are $-\infty$, choose both costs arbitrarily negative, so the product infimum is $-\infty$. If either is $+\infty$ and the other is not $-\infty$, the right side is $+\infty$ and the inequality is automatic. The mixed extended sum $+\infty+(-\infty)$ is undefined and is excluded by the Statement. [A1, F1, F2, construct]

1.3 A witness for $F(\Gamma\times C_0,\Gamma'\times C_0)$ is a witness for $F(\Gamma,\Gamma')$ with enlarged catalyst $C_0\times C$, so $F(\Gamma,\Gamma')\le F(\Gamma\times C_0,\Gamma'\times C_0)$. Conversely, add one fixed state of the nonempty catalyst $C_0$ to every edge of an arbitrary witness for $F(\Gamma,\Gamma')$. Its cost is unchanged, proving the reverse inequality. Thus $F(\Gamma\times C_0,\Gamma'\times C_0)=F(\Gamma,\Gamma')$. [A1, F1, F2]

2.1 Scaling every state, type, and catalyst in a witness by $t>0$ multiplies its cost by $t$ because $\sigma_{tT}(ta)=t\sigma_T(a)$. Each factor $[0,1]^d$ is Polish as a closed subspace of complete $\mathbb R^d$ with a countable dense rational grid; $\mathbb N_0$ with its discrete metric is Polish. The product exists by the finite product-measure theorem; each collision diagonal is null by Tonelli and the fact that Lebesgue measure gives every singleton measure zero, so the restricted measure still has mass one. Sorting is Borel on the finitely many permutation regions of the no-collision set. This defines a law $\pi_{i,\lambda}$ on $E_i$; for $n=0$, use the empty product and the empty configuration. ## Example
